Frontier AI models are now writing theoretical physics proofs and running massive 2.4-trillion parameter MoE architectures.

Here are the key technical developments in research, model scaling, and agentic systems from today.

🧠 Alibaba released Qwen4-Max, a 2.4-trillion parameter MoE model featuring 71B active parameters, native vision, and a 1M-token context window. It costs $1.5 per million input tokens and reduces Work360 cost per task by 62%.

🤖 Hark launched Handoff², a computer-use agent built for Hark Pro that averages 2x faster performance than v1. It completed 82% of 478 internal web tasks after learning to batch actions using latency-penalized reinforcement learning.

🔬 OpenAI shared progress on theoretical physics research, revealing that GPT-6 Astra helped convert a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model into a detailed proof.

📰 LVMH’s Media Division entered a strategic partnership with OpenAI to support journalism through AI integration and bring its publications directly into ChatGPT.

As models move from basic automation to advancing theoretical physics, the boundary of what AI can assist with is shifting into fundamental science.

Which capability do you think will impact developer workflows first: autonomous computer-use agents or massive 1M-context MoE models?
